transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-01-17 14:05 UTC
Duration: 38 mins
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Jonah (Redwood SE), Priya (ClearSight EM), Tomas (ClearSight Infra), Elena (ClearSight ML)

Summary:
Quick sync on access, VPC peering status, early benchmark results, and tuning next steps. Most of time on infra blockers and an anomaly in tail latency they saw during their internal runs. Agreed to run a repeat load test and exchange security docs.

Topics:
- VPC peering and credential handoff
- KV/prefix cache warmup and cold-start latency
- Batch configuration and quantization tradeoffs
- KMS/HSM and audit log retention
- Next benchmarks and timelines

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood): ok hey everyone thanks for jumping on, we'll run about 30 minutes, quick status and then Jonah can dive into tuning notes
[00:07] Priya (ClearSight): yes thanks Maya, we have limited time — Tomas had to handle a deployment so he might drop in and out
[00:12] Jonah (Redwood): no worries, I'll keep the deep stuff modular. so quick check: are you all seeing the same gate issue we saw in the ticket — VPC peering not yet established?
[00:20] Tomas (ClearSight): yeah correct, we had a rules mismatch on the transit VPC, firewall blocked the peer. I patched it yesterday but still seeing no handshake from the redwood side
[00:29] Maya (Redwood): hm okay, I think the tunnel didn't rotate the peer subnets. I'll re-run the peering script and share the debug logs.
[00:36] Priya: also one ask — we need service accounts limited to staging, not prod, can you scope that?
[00:40] Maya: yes we can do scoped tokens for the pilot, short-lived creds, nothing in prod.
[00:44] Elena (ClearSight): quick note on the benchmarks — our first run 2 days ago had decent p50 but we saw p99 spikes around 1.2s which is higher than expectation
[00:52] Jonah: ok can you describe the request shape — sequence length, batch size, and whether KV cache was used?
[00:58] Elena: sequence length avg ~220 tokens, some up to 600. We ran 20 concurrency, single request per session, we didn't warm any prefix cache — just cold start workloads
[01:10] Jonah: that explains a bit — long sequences plus cold KV cache will blow up tail. our runtime favors continuous batching and KV warmup; for your workload I'd recommend prefix caching for the common prompts and a small warmup sequence to populate the K-V store
[01:22] Priya: can you explain prefix caching quick — we heard KV cache but not sure of the tradeoffs
[01:28] Jonah: sure, prefix or prompt caching stores computed key-value pairs for repeated starts so subsequent requests avoid recomputing the early layers. tradeoff is memory; you need enough RAM on the worker and you want to evict rarely used prefixes. for short-lived prefix it helps a lot on p99
[01:40] Tomas: memory is tight on our staging gpus, we are on T4-equivalent nodes; Dedicated capacity might need A100s for big prefix cache?
[01:48] Maya: correct, quant + batching can help reduce mem but for heavy prefix caching A100/80GB is nicer. we can propose a Dedicated config for the pilot if you want predictable tail latency
[01:57] Priya: our budget is limited so first preference is hosted with good SLOs, but if we can't get p99 under 300ms we may consider a small dedicated pool
[02:07] Jonah: fair. two levers: batching profile and quantization. aggressive quant (4-bit) reduces cost and memory but sometimes adds error; for generation tail it can add a little variance. we can run an A/B with your prompt set
[02:20] Elena: how do we feed the prompt set? do you have a secure upload?
[02:24] Maya: yes, we'll share a secure S3 presigned workflow or you can drop into the redwood console private bucket — we'll redact anything PII before tests
[02:32] Tomas: about KMS — we use a customer-managed KMS in our region and need to verify key wrapping for inference tokens
[02:38] Jonah: Redwood supports bring-your-own-key via KMS or HSM — there are two modes, we can either wrap per-request tokens or use session keys. for your security posture I recommend perimeter key wrapping; I'll include the diagram in the security pack
[02:52] Priya: do you have SOC2 docs and ISO attestation? procurement asked earlier
[02:56] Maya: yes we'll attach SOC2 type II report and ISO summary, plus our standard audit-log retention options; I'll put them in the shared drive
[03:05] Elena: small transcription glitch — sorry the tool we used shows some mis-typed prompt names, ignore that
[03:09] Maya: np, thanks. Jonah, what specific tuning steps should Elena try first for the repeat run?
[03:14] Jonah: start 1) reduce sequence length where possible via prompt clipping; 2) enable a small shared prefix cache for the top 10 prompts; 3) increase batch size slightly to 8 or 12 depending on latency under load; 4) try 8-bit quant first (q8) then 4-bit (q4) only if accuracy holds. I'll send an example profiles.json
[03:35] Elena: OK will do. one more question on telemetry — can we forward traces to our datadog?
[03:40] Maya: yes, we have a tracing hook and can forward spans; for pilot we usually send token-level latencies and model traces to their telemetry endpoint, you can opt-in to full token traces or aggregated metrics only
[03:52] Tomas: what's the recommended retention for audit logs during the POC? procurement asked for 90 days minimum
[03:58] Maya: default is 30 days on hosted, but for pilot we can extend to 90 days as an add-on. for private you control retention in your VPC
[04:07] Priya: on the peering front — Tomas patched the firewall but we still see the handshake missing. can you confirm which CIDRs Redwood expects?
[04:14] Jonah: we expect three ranges: control plane, data plane, and peering control. I'll paste the exact list in a follow-up but likely it's a firewall rule mismatch or NAT issue
[04:24] Tomas: got it — I'll pull NAT gateway logs and share.
[04:28] Elena: we saw a weird regression during one test where throughput dropped at 75% utilization — might be batching hysteresis?
[04:35] Jonah: that sounds like autothrottle/batch sizing oscillation. we have a parameter that controls batch aggregation window and a cooldown; when utilization climbs you can tune the window to avoid thrash. I'll include recommended values
[04:46] Priya: can you also share a cost delta for switching to dedicated 2xA100 vs hosted peak bursts? procurement needs a rough delta today
[04:54] Maya: yes, I'll prepare a short table — committed vs burst pricing — expect dedicated to be ~3-4x higher for reserved but lower per-token under sustained throughput. hosted is better for intermittent load
[05:06] Elena: about warmup — any scripts we should run to prime the KV cache before a big spike?
[05:11] Jonah: yes we have a warmup runner that replays a set of prompts at low concurrency to populate prefix keys. run for 30-60 seconds before planned blast. I'll attach the script
[05:20] Tomas: do you support SAML/SSO for console access? we want RBAC so devs can't touch infra creds
[05:26] Maya: yes SAML SSO, SCIM provisioning for groups, and RBAC roles. we'll provide the metadata file and example mapping
[05:33] Priya: any blockers for us to reach feature parity vs the in-house infra we built? we worry about feature gaps, e.g., custom model hooks
[05:40] Jonah: we support function/tool calling and custom model variants; for heavy model editing you can bring a model artifact to our private deployment. for the pilot you should be fine to test standard generation and embeddings
[05:50] Maya: ok let's recap and next steps
[05:52] Maya (recap): 1) Redwood to send security pack, VPC CIDRs and peering checklist, SAML metadata. 2) Jonah to send tuning guide, warmup script, and example profiles. 3) ClearSight to run 50-user latency test with the prompt set and share telemetry. 4) schedule follow-up 30-min and decide whether hosted SLOs suffice or we propose a small Dedicated pool.
[06:12] Priya: agree. thanks everyone.
[06:15] Tomas: thanks, I'll post NAT logs and confirm firewall rules by tomorrow.
[06:19] Elena: thanks, I'll start the run tonight and upload artifacts.
[06:22] Maya: great, we'll follow up with docs and a date for the follow-up.
[06:26] [call ends]

Notes on transcription: occasional speaker label swaps at 02:56 and 04:35; some product names transcribed as "red wood" or "K V cache" instead of "Redwood" and "KV cache".
